plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than to competitors, and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid, which will always be at or below my value if I win.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid my true value of $44, I win whenever the highest competing bid is below $44, and I pay whatever that second-highest bid is—never more than my value allows for profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $44 to maximize expected profit.

In this second-price auction format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than the price I'll pay, and I never overpay. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item's worth to me if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $43.
